primitives.name: Play Distribution Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: FOOT-BALL IN AMERICA 123 plays should not be all alike, but all directed at this one point, and played in as rapid succession as possible.
primitives.assumptions: All plays converge toward a single objective; rapid succession reduces opponent adaptation time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When all plays are identical, opponent predictive models become highly accurate.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to multi-armed bandit optimization where each play type is a reward arm with diminishing returns if overused.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of unique play usage per game segment

primitives.name: Runner Freshness Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The same man should not be made the runner by the assaulting team, but kept fresh by the variation of their action, and throwing the hardest work successively upon different men, while the same two or three men of the opponents are forced to meet it.
primitives.assumptions: Player fatigue reduces performance efficiency; rotational strategy maintains peak output.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a single player is overused, performance degradation becomes exponential.

layer2.mapping: Derived from fatigue kernel applied to player-specific action profiles; modeled as inverse linear decay in effectiveness.
layer2.telemetry: Average time between consecutive runs per player

primitives.name: Ball Loss Risk Assessment
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is one other vital point which should be always borne in mind by the captain when using his plays in a game, and that is the possibility of an accidental loss of the ball.
primitives.assumptions: Accidental ball loss introduces stochastic failure mode with high impact in critical zones.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Risk increases exponentially near opponent goal lines due to reduced recovery margin.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to error propagation model in control systems; failure probability scales with spatial proximity to scoring zone.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of plays executed within 25-yard line

The core insight of play distribution optimization lies in maximizing collective efficacy through strategic rotation—each play must serve a unified tactical aim yet vary in execution to prevent predictability. This aligns with information-theoretic principles where entropy in action space correlates with uncertainty reduction in opponent modeling. Runner freshness is a derived consequence of this principle: sustained effort without rotation leads to diminishing returns, modeled as a fatigue kernel. The interplay between these two primitives creates a dual constraint: increasing diversity of execution while preserving individual capability. Ball loss risk assessment introduces a stochastic element that modifies the utility landscape—particularly near goal lines, where even small deviations can yield catastrophic outcomes. These constraints form a bounded optimization problem where the objective function balances offensive aggression against defensive stability. The failure modes emerge from violations of these constraints: over-reliance on singular strategies, neglect of player conditioning, and reckless risk-taking in vulnerable zones.
